name: Desk Terminal, Vera Card
tagline: Gauged Rows with Home opening on one Vera card (greeting, a glass strip for the question and a lit Listening line, the box) beside a bezelled Next up tube on a grid floor.
concept: The parent's terminal split in two. The greeting, the typed question, the status line and the box, which shared one tall column with the tube, become one graphite Vera card with a lit top-left corner. Next up and its chart move to a bezelled tube beside it, standing on a perspective grid floor, so Home's first screen reads as a person talking and a monitor answering. The status line is now a lit strip with a breathing lamp, "Listening" in bright phosphor, the plans watched dim after it, and one tick per plan at the right.
companions: Nothing new. The card uses the parent's graphite body with its indigo wash in the top-right corner, the steel hairline under the speaker row, and the heading ink for her name. Amber (people) is only the retrying/lost state of the status strip. Sage and steel-cyan are untouched. #6dff9c stays on the card's lit corner, the lamp, "mind", Send and the tube.
decisions: GLASS: the donor's idea (one Vera card beside a bezelled tube with a grid floor) is built in the parent's materials. It sits in a new `glass` block in base.html above the terminal and the desk, so Home's grid gets a full-width first row. The terminal under it keeps the Contents plate and the status foot. The Tab order is the card's form, then the tube's links, then the terminal, then the desk. On a phone the card comes first, then the tube.

The question stays typed on lit glass (principle 20). The donor sets it in Archivo on a plain plate, but here it stays VT323 on a recessed strip of glass inside the card, with scanlines, vignette and the phosphor text-shadow of the tube. This keeps the 'machine speaks on glass' rule, and the strip is what makes the card read as the parent's, not the donor's.
The apostrophe in What's is set in Plex Mono (`.apos`) because VT323's curly apostrophe is the known tall-tick fault, and it is much more visible at 44px than at 32px.

SIGNAL: the parent already had a status line, so this goes further. The line becomes a full-width strip at the foot of the glass with a hairline above it and a phosphor gradient behind it. It has a 14px lamp whose ring breathes outward, 'Listening' in bright uppercase, 'watching 4 plans' dim, and one lit tick per plan watched at the right, with the next plan's tick taller. Thinking speeds the lamp up, and retrying or lost turn the strip amber with a steady lamp. The ticks make the count a readable shape, and it is still decided by code from the log with no model call.

TYPE: the parent's body already set at 1.55, so the change reaches the prose that did not. Muted lines, hints, ledes, band notes, descriptions, summaries, state lines and chat text all get 1.55 leading and a 66ch cap. Panels, rows, errors, notices and the glass are excluded so no box shrinks and no row misaligns.

The grid floor is the donor's perspective grid, redrawn in the tube's phosphor at 38% and masked to fade upward. It fills the glass the chart does not use, and the chart is switched to its `tall` form so the tube is mostly drawing and not empty.
measures: ink_on_bg 12.61, brand_on_bg 14.89. Green share of colour: home 53.3%, ideas 33.0%, chat 55.7%, status 32.2%. Hue entropy: home 0.635, ideas 0.564, chat 0.493, status 0.515. Kinds/sections dE typical/deutan/protan: kinds 13.6/5.5/7.4, sections 13.3/5.4/5.3. Greeting corner pixel (1150,120) is (4,12,8), now the dark glass of the tube. The old wash corner is dark glass and the sample at (100,640) is (12,20,24). 0 hard fails. One WARN: the page's words differ from today's (worst 38% on plans, 19.1% on home), which is inherited from the parent's markup.
strengths: Home's first screen now has two clear parts: a card to talk to Vera and a monitor showing what is next. This is a bigger change in the page's structure than a restyle.
The status strip is a real signal. The lamp, the lit word and the ticks give the same information three ways, it keeps the parent's amber/steady/breathing states, and it needs no model call.
The question stays on lit glass at the top of Home, so the page keeps its green-screen identity.
Every other page is identical to the parent, so the slot differences are clean.
weaknesses: The terminal now holds only the Contents plate and status foot, so in a full-page shot there is a long empty stretch below it in the left column on Home. It is sticky in use, but the cards show the void.

The tube is taller than its content because it stretches to the card's height. The grid floor and the `tall` chart fill it, but the glass still has some spare room above the floor. The grid floor is close to the 'Tron floor' costume the lessons warned about, so it is kept faint.

The TYPE change is hard to see on the half-size cards. The parent's body was already at 1.55, so the visible part is the 66ch cap and the leading on muted lines. The effect is on Settings and Status prose.
On a phone the status line wraps to two lines, and the card plus the tube make Home's first screen long before the first band.
Plex Mono for the apostrophe is a small patch over a VT323 flaw. It may look slightly off up close beside the pixel letters.
The card adds a rounded second 'machine' on Home. Principle 9 wanted one cased terminal, so this goes against it on purpose.

elements.what: `{% block glass %}` in variants/r18-mut-1/templates/home.html, hung off a new empty block in base.html. `.vera-row` holds `.vera-card` (speaker row `.vera-top`, glass strip `.vera-glass`, box `.vera-deck` with _ask.html) and a `crt('next-up tube-home vera-tube')` with `.tube-floor`. CSS is in r18.css under GLASS.

`.glass-status` in home.html's `.vera-glass` (`.gs-lamp`, `.gs-words`, `.gs-pips`): a lit strip with a breathing lamp and ring, 'Listening' lit, the plans watched dim, and one tick per plan. Amber when retrying or lost. CSS is under SIGNAL in r18.css.

The last rule block in r18.css: `main :is(p.muted, p.hint, .lede, .why, .description, .said-text, .band-note, .section-state, ...)` sets line-height 1.55 and max-width 66ch, leaving out panels, rows, errors and notices. It is page-wide and self-contained.

name: Desk Terminal, Scanned Case
tagline: Gauged Rows with the key word drawn through raster lines under a bloom, prose leading at 1.55 on a 66-character measure, and a thin bezel inset with one row of vents on the terminal case.
concept: The parent (Desk Terminal, Gauged Rows) with three small changes and nothing else. The question's key word "mind" is drawn as a tube draws it, raster lines through a white-hot-to-phosphor gradient with a three-halo bloom, so it is the brightest thing on the glass. Prose gets a steadier 1.55 leading and a 66-character cap. The graphite case gets a recessed groove with a lip just inside its edge and a row of vent slots across the top.
companions: Unchanged from the parent. Sage #86d9a6 for lit, done and outing. Steel-cyan #a0bccb for here, links and plate names. Section hairlines on the bands. The new bloom uses only the exact #6dff9c with a white-hot core. The case groove and vents are black and graphite highlights, with no new hue.
decisions: Light: lifted r16-wild-1's .glow (raster lines through a gradient clipped to the glyphs, drop-shadow halos, text-shadow fallback under @supports) onto the parent's .ask-question .glow, which was already a white-hot word. Fidelity changes here: the donor's 17rem display type had room for 3px stripes in the strokes. VT323 strokes at about 38px are only 2 to 3px, so 4px-period stripes at 0.6 black dimmed the word below its neighbours. I settled on 1px of 0.36 black every 4px, a lighter gradient (near white to #6dff9c) and the word at 1.45em, so the stripes read and the word stays brightest.

Kept the glow list short. No glow was added anywhere else. The parent already lights only its live things (NOW rail and lamp, status lamp, tube, Send), so the donor's 'glow only on live things' needed no further change.

Reduced-contrast and print fallbacks: with prefers-contrast: more or print the clipped fill is replaced by a solid phosphor or dark green with no filter, because a transparent clipped fill would otherwise vanish.

Type: the parent's body was already 1.55. What is raised to 1.55 is the prose that sat at 1.45 to 1.6 (.lede, .said-text, .her .lede, .section-state, .description, .hint, .small and the paragraphs in bands, desks and panels). Their measure is capped at 66ch. This widens the 58 to 62ch caps on .lede, .said-text and .description by a few characters, which is what a literal 66 cap implies. It narrows the uncapped hints and notes.

Glass: the bezel inset is an outline (2px black at 0.7, offset -5px) plus a ::before lip under it, so the groove follows the rounded case and does not scroll away inside the sticky overflow terminal. The vent row is a ::after with 20 slots about 9rem wide, centred on the top edge. Top padding is 1.75rem so the vents have their own strip. The case exists only at 64rem and wider (below that the terminal is display: contents), so all of it is inside that media query.
Everything else (tokens, markup, templates, other CSS) is byte-for-byte the parent's. The parent's css is carried unchanged and the three blocks are appended in variants/r18-mut-2/r18.css.
measures: ./check.sh full render: 0 hard failures, 1 WARN, the page-words share (worst plans 38.0%, home 19.1%), which is inherited from the parent's markup and dates, not from these changes. ink_on_bg 12.61, brand_on_bg 14.89. Green share of colour 45.2% on home and 31.5% on status. Hue entropy 0.673 on home and 0.528 on status. Bright green 4.04 permille on home. Kinds dE typical 13.6, deutan 5.5, protan 7.4. Sections dE typical 13.3, deutan 5.4, protan 5.3. Greeting corner pixels, top right (30,36,40) and bottom left (33,45,52). No sideways scroll. Smallest text 12px.
strengths: The key word is now the one lit, textured thing on Home: raster lines and a bloom make the tube read as a tube, and it is brighter than everything near it. That brings back the original phosphor effect without adding glare elsewhere.
The case reads as hardware on every page that has a terminal. The vent row and groove are black and graphite only, so no new colour comes in.
Chat bubbles, ledes and Status hints get a steadier rhythm. The slightly wider 66ch measure helps long sentences on the desk.
Each change has its own classes (.ask-question .glow, a prose selector list, .terminal::before and ::after) and is lifted out in r18.css.
weaknesses: The raster stripes on 'mind' are visible at 100% but close to invisible on the half-size cards. What the cards show is the bigger word, the near-white core and the halo.
The word is whiter than the exact #6dff9c, since only the gradient's bottom is brand. The signature green is not the face of the key word.
The type change is subtle. The parent's body was already 1.55, so only the prose that was at 1.45 to 1.6 moves, and the 66ch cap widens some 58 to 62ch blocks by a few characters.
The groove is a thin dark line. It can be missed on a half-size card, and the vents add about 12px to every terminal's height.
On the phone and below 64rem there is no case, so the glass change does not appear there.

elements.what: Scanlined bloom on the key word: `.ask-question .glow` in variants/r18-mut-2/r18.css (home.html's `mind`). Repeating-linear-gradient raster lines over a near-white-to-#6dff9c gradient, clipped to the glyphs, three drop-shadow halos, a text-shadow fallback under @supports, and prefers-contrast and print fallbacks.

Prose at 1.55 leading and a 66ch measure: one selector list in r18.css (.lede, .said-text, .her .lede, .section-state, .description, .lead, .why, .hint, .small, .step-skip-note, .capture > p, and paragraphs in .desk, .band, .panel, .contents and .status-foot).

A thin bezel inset and a vent row on the case: `.terminal` (outline groove at offset -5px, extra top padding) with `.terminal::before` (the lip under the groove) and `.terminal::after` (the slotted vent row), all inside @media (min-width: 64rem) in r18.css; base.html's `<aside class="terminal">` is unchanged.

name: Track Diagram Scanlined
tagline: Track Diagram Aglow with the key word drawn as a tube draws it, scanlines through a green gradient with a two-halo bloom, glow kept to the live things, keys set in a recessed tray with a lit radio dot and a raised bright Add key, and body text at 1.55 with a 66-character measure.
concept: Parent r18-head-1 with three changes. The one question word ("mind") is now drawn the way a tube draws it: raster lines through a green gradient clipped to the glyph, with a layered drop-shadow bloom, enlarged so the lines show. The filters become a recessed tray holding raised keycaps, each with a radio ring that lights on the one in force, and the Add key is a taller raised green key. Reading text sits on one 1.55 leading and stops at 66 characters. The feeling is the same calm, grounded desk with one lit word.
companions: Unchanged from the parent. Steel #a7c4d8 is the accent, for links, the "here" key cap and the title tiles. Cream #efe3cf is the heading. Slate #161c20 and tray #0f1519 hold the controls. Lilac, cyan, lemon, amber, pink and coral stay on their own pages. Amber still marks late and needs-a-look. No new colour was added.
decisions: [light] The key word `.glow` gets a repeating scanline gradient over a gradient that runs from brand-hover through the exact #6dff9c to a slightly deeper green, clipped with background-clip:text. Three stacked drop-shadows give the bloom, and an @supports guard keeps the plain two-layer text-shadow where clipping is missing. The donor's gradient colours were not copied; every stop is a mix of the parent's --brand and --brand-hover.

[light] The parent's key word was only 1.4rem, so 3px scanlines would not have shown. On Home the word and its '?' are set 1.75em, weight 800, with the '?' wrapped in `.q-mark` (a one-line edit to templates/_ask.html) at 70% opacity. The label's clip-path is widened so the bloom is not cut, and the typed-question cursor is re-anchored to the baseline of the larger word. Chat's `.open-q .glow` takes the same scanlines at its own size.

[light] Glow is kept for live things. The parent already lights its rails, NOW lamps, lamps, mark and tube, so those are untouched. The matte changes are the accent halo round the title-icon tiles and the drop-shadow on the bar's current icon and menu icon, which are not live. Reduced-contrast, print and forced-colors reset the clipped fill to a plain colour.

[controls] Same idea, more of it. `.key-row` becomes a recessed tray (inset shadow, tray fill) holding keycaps with a lighter top edge, a 2px base shadow and a 4px radius. Every filter link carries a hollow radio ring on the right, and the key in force is pressed 2px down, with a steel top cap and a larger lit lamp-core dot. The ring tells the family at a glance that these are choices. Keys stay at 2.75rem tall, and the tray sits inside a fit-content width so it does not stretch.

[controls] `.head-add` is taller (2.9rem), weight 700, with a bright gradient fill, a darker-green base edge that makes it a raised key, a wider halo, a lift on hover and a press-down on active. Its icon is a little bolder.

[type] The body leading is set to 1.55 (the parent's was 1.6, so this is a unification and a slight tightening, not a rise). The reading blocks that sat tighter than that (.lede, .description, .hint, .muted, .empty, .section-state, .card p and similar) go up to 1.55. `main p` and the reading classes are capped at 66ch, with exceptions for the status line, key labels and monitor text. Chat's .said-text, which was 64ch, becomes 66ch.
measures: The full ./check.sh run has 0 hard failures and one guideline miss, the share of words that differ from today (19% on Plans, the parent's own wording; the only wording change I made is none, the '?' wrap adds no words). ink_on_bg 12.57, brand_on_bg 14.96, brand_neon_vs_today 1.0, glow, screenGlow and topGlow all 1.0. Home: green share of colour 63.3%, hue entropy 0.536. Ideas: green share 47.7%, hue entropy 0.478. Kinds dE typical 13.6, deutan 5.5, protan 7.4. Sections dE typical 12.8, deutan 5.5, protan 5.3. Greeting corner pixels: top right (24,34,46), bottom left (15,21,25). Bright-green pixels per mille: Home 3.52, Ideas 8.26. Smallest text 11.52px.
strengths: The key word is clearly different at 100%: lit scanlines and a layered bloom on a larger heavy word, still the exact #6dff9c at its core, and it reads as a tube word, not an effect on the page.

The filters get more physical and easier to read. The tray with raised caps and a hollow ring that lights on the choice makes Ideas, To do and Plans controls plainly choice-and-state on the half-size cards.
The bright raised Add key is a stronger primary action in Ideas' head.
Nothing else moved, so the slots can be told apart: no colours, tokens, markup structure or the parent's glows on live things changed.
weaknesses: The scanlines are fine (3px period), so on the half-size Home card the word reads as bigger and brighter more than as scanlined. The lines only show on the 100% close card.

The type roll asked to raise leading to 1.55, but the parent's body was already 1.6, so the net change is a slight tightening plus the lifting of tighter secondary text. The 66ch cap bites only on a few long paragraphs (Settings help, the setup text), so it will be hard for a judge to see.
The scanline gradient lowers the word's average brightness a little, and a light-mode `-webkit-background-clip` fallback is untested in browsers other than this Chromium.
Making the Home question's lit word 1.75x its neighbours changes the greeting's rhythm. The h1 now has two sizes, which some judges may call a stretch of the type slot.
The filter trays add roughly 8px of height per key row, so the Ideas filter panel is a little taller. The ring on every link key widens the keys, so the Kind row now wraps to two lines.
Quieting the title-tile and nav-icon halos removes some light that the 'bring the phosphor back' owner may miss; the gain is only a clearer split between live and matte.

name: Track Diagram Index Folio
tagline: Track Diagram Dial Keys with Lit Index's head: a folio in the section's colour over a giant condensed title, its count on the same baseline, the deck beside it and one hairline with a short section bar under it; the ground a step cooler, the bone neutrals a step warmer, the glass question one step smaller.
concept: The parent's ring-and-elbow head is replaced by an index head on every page: a mono folio (02 Ideas, 03 Plans, 04 To do, C Status, D Settings) in the page's colour, the title set giant in Archivo at its narrowest and heaviest in warm bone, the parent's typed count standing beside it on the same baseline, the deck in a second column on that baseline, and a hairline under the whole head with a 3px bar of the section's colour at its left. Only Chat keeps its ring, as the terminus of the thread line that hangs from it. The page feels like a printed index with a lit machine under it: a bigger, calmer first read of where you are, over a ground that has cooled a step and ink that has warmed a step.
companions: Unchanged from the parent. Steel #a7c4d8 is the accent, so the folio, short bar and count are steel on Home, Status and Settings, and the section's own colour elsewhere (lilac Ideas, cyan Plans, lemon To do, amber Family and Memory, pink Wishes). The labels stay steel. Bone is the neutral, now one step warmer. Green stays on the live things only (mark, Send, key word, focus, tubes, lamps).
decisions: Head: I took Lit Index's structure (folio, giant condensed title, brass hairline with a short section bar, deck on the baseline, one action at the right) and drew it in the parent's materials. The hairline is the parent's steel label colour mixed 42% into the ground, the folio and bar use --accent, the title uses --heading, and the count is the parent's own typed figure, so the page does not lose its counts (donor had none). Everything is scoped to .page-head.ix and its own classes.

The head markup moved in _ui.html's page_head. The deck now lives inside .page-title so it can sit on the title's baseline in a flex row that wraps it under the title when there is no room (Status, with the dial tube at the right). The ring and rail are rendered only when the glyph is 'presence' (Chat), so the thread line keeps its origin. Folio numbers are body-class custom properties, so no extra markup is needed.
I removed the two palette rules that placed Status's deck in the old head grid, since that grid no longer exists.

Chat keeps the grid with the ring column and no bottom rule, so the thread line runs down from the ring. Its title is capped at 4.6rem so the thread starts in the first screen. On phones the ring's vertical stub is dropped.

Colour roll: the ground goes from #081111 to #071116 (hue 196 to 230) and the neutrals warm one step: ink #ddd0bb to #e5d3b5, ink-2 #c8b99e, dim #b2a186, faint #a29379, heading #f3e4cc. The parent's sheet.css bakes its own copy of these tokens, which overrode the palette's, so I changed them in both (and the bar's rgb(7 17 22/.82)). The first attempt at #071113 (hue 211) was invisible on the cards, so I went to #071116. The surfaces, lines and bar keep the parent's slate, so only the black behind them cools.

Glass roll: the parent already blinked the cursor only while the box is focused, with a steady dim block at rest, so I kept that and took the question one more step down, from clamp(1.15rem,2vw,1.4rem) to clamp(1rem,1.6vw,1.2rem) (22px to 19px at desktop width). The lit key word 'mind' is unchanged.
measures: Full render: 0 hard checks failed, 2 WARN. (1) bg is no longer green-black: OKLCH L 0.170, C 0.018, hue 230 against the 115-200 guideline; this is the cooler-ground roll. (2) Words differ from today by 19.0% on Plans, which is identical to the parent (head-1 gives the same figure), so the head change added no words. ink_on_bg 13.01, brand_on_bg 14.93, heading on bg 15.3. brand and screen are exactly #6dff9c, with L 0.897, C 0.186, h 151.4. Green share of colour: home 61.7%, ideas 73.8%, chat 74.9%, status 79.6%. Hue entropy: home 0.539, ideas 0.489, chat 0.405, status 0.407. Kinds dE typ/deu/pro 13.6/5.5/7.4; sections 12.8/5.5/5.3 (all pass). Smallest text 11.52px. No sideways scroll. Greeting corner pixels: top right (24,34,46), bottom left (15,21,25), unchanged from the parent; ground sample (7,17,22).
strengths: The head change shows on every page card (Ideas, Plans, To do, Status, Settings, Chat) at half size: giant condensed bone titles with a coloured folio and short bar are the strongest page-wide change in the set.
The count is kept. The donor had none, so the graft keeps the parent's typed figure and its unit and change line, standing on the same baseline as the title.
The deck wraps under the title when there is no room, so the Status page with its dial tube and the phone need no special cases.
Chat keeps its thread origin, so the track-diagram idea survives where it carries meaning.
Self-contained: .ix classes, the folio as body-class variables, and no change to anything but the head's markup and CSS.
weaknesses: Archivo condensed is a fifth face beside Fraunces h2s, Plex Sans and Mono, and VT323. The digest warns about four or more faces, and the serif section heads under a sans poster title are a visible pairing seam.

The cooler ground is barely visible on the half-size cards. It is a few RGB steps, and it breaks the green-black hue guideline (hue 230 against a limit of 200), so the cooling costs signature points for a small gain. The warmer ink is also subtle.

The glass tweak is the parent's own tweak taken one step further. The question is now about 19px and quieter beside the monitor, which cuts against the principle that the machine's question is the page's largest head on Home.
The head loses the page-icon ring on every page except Chat, so the section icon now appears only in the bar and tabs, and the track-diagram line no longer starts at the head.
The hairline under the head is still faint on the cards, and the folio is only 14px, so the folio nearly disappears at half size; on Status the tall dial tube leaves a void above the title.
Phone heads were not rendered (the harness shoots only Home on the phone). They are checked by reasoning, not by sight.

elements.what: Index head. The page_head macro in variants/r18-mut-4/templates/_ui.html emits header.page-head.ix > .ix-title > .ix-row (h1 plus .head-count) + .lede, plus .page-actions. The CSS block is headed 'HEAD' in the palette css. It is made of: a folio from body.in-<section> custom properties on .ix-title::before, h1 in Archivo wdth 62 at weight 800 and up to 5.25rem, a hairline border-bottom plus a 5.5rem 3px ::after bar in --accent, and the deck in a flex-wrapping second column. The ring and rail appear only for the chat (.has-ring).

Cooler ground and warmer bone neutrals. Tokens bg #071116 and ink/ink-2/dim/faint/heading #e5d3b5/#c8b99e/#b2a186/#a29379/#f3e4cc, set in the palette and in the :root block at the top of sheet.css (which bakes the same tokens and would otherwise win), plus the bar's translucent rgb(7 17 22/.82).

The Home ask-box question one size smaller: the last rule of the palette css, .ask-question{font-size:clamp(1rem,1.6vw,1.2rem)}. The block cursor stays dim and steady at rest and blinks only under .ask:focus-within (inherited from the parent, kept).

name: Lit Index, Ruled Rail
tagline: Lit Index with the chat thread hung on a brass rail from Vera's mark, checkboxes drawn as lit squares in an empty frame, and a primary key whose press throws echoing rings that fade.
concept: The parent, r18-head-2 (Lit Index), carried unchanged except for three slots. The Chat thread now hangs on a 2px brass rail that starts at Vera's mark. Times sit in the left margin and the family's lines arrive at a ring on the rail along a dotted leader. The rail ends at the box in a lit green ring, "your turn". Checkboxes are an empty frame that lights one small square when ticked. The Send key's press throws two rings outward and fades over about 1.7 seconds.
companions: The parent's, unchanged. Brass (the label token) draws the rail, the times and the dotted leaders. Amber (people) marks the family's bubbles, with a 3px right edge on the family's side. Lit sage (#86d9a6) is the left edge of Vera's bubbles and her "asks" label. The #6dff9c brand appears only on the end-of-rail ring, the glowing "mind" in the thread opener, and the key's press light.
decisions: [chat] Grafted r17-mut-10's rail but redrew it in the parent's materials. It keeps the parent's single-column page and its giant Vera head. The rail is brass (label colour mixed with bg), bubbles use the parent's bubble and bubble-them fills with its 3px tab edge, and the corners are the parent's 3px. Donor colours (steel, serif) are not used.

[chat] The donor's serif question became the parent's Archivo (wdth 84, 700) at 2rem. The parent's giant lit .glow is reset inside .open-q so it stays one lit word. This adds a 'Vera asks / What's on your mind?' opener to the Chat page, about 6 words more than the parent.

[chat] The margin times were wrapping onto two lines in the first render. I fixed the .hang width and set nowrap. Phone (max 40rem): margin times and the leader are hidden, the time shows inline in the speaker line, and the rail narrows. The harness does not shoot a phone Chat, so this was not checked by eye.

[light] The parent's key-afterglow (one halo flare, 1.1s) became key-echo, 1.7s: two expanding box-shadow rings (4px to 9px to 14px to 20px) plus the halo and a brightness flare, fading to rest. Only primary keys, same selector as the parent. Reduced motion turns the animation off. It shows in the Focus 1st Tab crop on SEND. A mouse press cannot be seen in a still.

[controls] Checkbox off: transparent fill and a thin 1.5px edge frame. On: the frame turns lit and a 0.62rem square lights inside, with an outer bloom and inner glow, and no tick mark. An earlier tick background-image rule hid the square at first. I set background-image explicitly on :checked and :checked:focus.

[controls] The task tick button is the same box, so on hover or focus a half-lit square appears instead of the check icon. That is a small extension of the same idea, so the To do list and the checkboxes agree.
Everything else is byte-identical to the parent (palette tokens, glow numbers, all other templates). The only template changes are chat.html and the chat_line macro in _ui.html.
measures: The final full render reports 0 hard checks failed and 1 guideline missed. The miss is the words-unchanged guideline, worst on the login page at 17.2% differing. I did not measure the parent on that line, so I do not know how much of the 17.2% is mine. Home is the parent's card unchanged: ink_on_bg 15.9, brand_on_bg 15.28, brand_neon_vs_today 1.0, glow, screenGlow and topGlow 1.0. The Plans list view, Status lights, Settings cells and wishes were not converted, so 'every list row' is only true for five lists. Plans list was not rendered at all.
The head is bigger in the left-hand Chat column, where Vera plus a large figure is a little crowded. On Status the title sits low because the spend gauge shares the head.
The Chat card only just fits the 900px viewport shot, thanks to a trimmed thread gap and a 3.7rem box. With a longer thread the composer drops below the fold, as it did before.
The new 'breathing' ring is a small live animation, and it stays lit under reduced motion.
The deck now sits below the rule on every page, which adds a line's height under the title on pages with short ledes.

elements.what: Counted folio head: _ui.html page_head puts the lede in p.lede.deck after header.page-head.has-deck. CSS block '[head] THE COUNTED FOLIO' scales .page-head .title-row h1 and .hc-figure, with .hc-unit as the small unit, over the head's hairline ::after rule, and sets .lede.deck under it.

Lit rail plus Vera card: chat.html block '.your-turn.vera-card' (.turn-head with .speaker and .glass-status, the include of _ask.html with chips, .turn-now). CSS block '[chat] MORE OF THE RAIL' holds the 3px lit .thread.line::before, larger .stamp times, the 22px breathing ring on .your-turn.vera-card::after and the fitted card rules.

Tight rows with a right-aligned tabular facts column: CSS block '[list] ROWS ONE STEP TIGHTER' with --row-pad and --facts-w, on .bank.coming > .cells.agenda, .bank.home-todo > .cells.checklist, .bank.lately > .cells.idea-cards, .bank.ideas-bank > ul.cards.cells and .bank.tasks-bank > ul.cards.cells. tasks.html moves .card-id into .task-head.

name: Grid Console Folio Head
tagline: Grid Console Cream Rail with a giant condensed title over a mono running head and folio, a cooler blue-slate ground with warmer cream-and-peach type, and the first word of every row's label set medium.
concept: Each page opens like a printed index. A small mono running head (icon, folio 00-05 or A-D, and the page's count) sits over a very large condensed cream title, with the lede in a second column on its baseline. Under it the existing light trail gets a short 3px bar of the page's colour at its left. The ground leans a step toward blue and the cream type a step toward peach, and every row label reads first word medium, rest regular. It feels like a clean, indexed instrument panel.
companions: Unchanged from the parent: the teal-cyan accent #77ced5 carries the folio, bar and trail on Chat, Status and Settings. The section colours (lilac Ideas, cyan Plans, lemon To do, amber Family and Memory, pink Wishes) colour each page's folio, icon, count figure and 3px bar. Sage #86d9a6 is still the lit colour, the amber count change line still marks "late" or "needs a look", and #6dff9c stays on the mark, Send, the key word, focus and the monitors.
decisions: HEAD: I used the lifted Lit Index element (giant condensed title, folio, rule) and drew it in the parent's materials. The title is Archivo wdth 62 at weight 800 in the heading cream, up to 5rem (80px, below Lit Index's 5.5rem). The folio is Martian Mono in the page's colour. The rule is the parent's own light trail with a 3px section bar added at its left, not Lit Index's brass hairline. The parent's spine and elbow still attach to it.

HEAD: the parent's big underlined typed count would have competed with a giant title, so I demoted it to a running-head readout beside the folio: a mono figure in the page's colour, a small-caps unit, and the amber change line. Every figure, unit and change word is kept, so the page's words are unchanged. The small icon tile becomes a plain 1.1rem icon at the start of the running head. Vera's screen stays beside her name on Chat.

HEAD: the old single-line-head and typed-count CSS blocks are deleted from the sheet and replaced by one [head] block at the end. The title's serif rule was parent type, which this head replaces for page titles only; h2, card titles and record names keep the parent's serif.

COLOUR: the roll was ground one step cooler and neutrals one step warmer. The ground tokens (surfaces, fields, lines, edge, card-edge, bubbles, bezel) moved +17 degrees of hue toward blue-slate with 18% more chroma. The bg and bar are #031415, held at the signature's hue-200 edge (199.95), so they are still a green-black rather than blue. The neutrals (ink, ink-2, dim, faint, heading, secondary) moved -11 degrees toward peach with 30% more chroma at unchanged lightness, so contrast is unchanged. The first attempt, a few degrees, would not have shown on half-size cards, so I made it bolder.

LIST: the parent already carried this roll as a `.lead` word at weight 500, but a later type rule (`.card h2` at 620) made the first word lighter than the rest in cards, so it was broken there. Fixed by moving the rule to the end of the sheet and setting rest 400, lead 580. The span.lead reset removes the old `.lead` paragraph rule's 1.04rem size and ink-2 colour, which shrank the first word. Coverage is extended with the `lead` macro to Status's lamp labels, Home's setup steps and the plans month's events, so the rule holds on every page.
Palette signature kept: brand and screen exactly #6dff9c, screenGlow and glow 1.0.
measures: ink_on_bg 12.84, brand_on_bg 14.74. Green share of colour: home 65.2, ideas 42.9, chat 44.2, status 56.5 (percent). Hue entropy: home 0.53, ideas 0.535, chat 0.518, status 0.45. dE typical/deutan/protan: kinds 15.4/5.4/8.6, sections 15.4/5.4/8.2. Greeting corner pixels on Home: top right (1150,120) is (4,9,6) and bottom left (100,640) is (13,25,30). 0 hard checks failed. One guideline WARN: words changed on Plans (16.5%), which I did not cause.
strengths: The giant condensed title is the strongest hierarchy step on every page. It is clearly visible at half size and reads as an index page, with the folio, count and lede fitting one grid.
The head is a system, not an effect. Folio and section colour come from the body class, so Plans, To do, Settings and Memory all follow the same rule without new markup.
The cooler ground and warmer type show at a glance on every page, not only in a corner, and the signature (bg hue under 200, brand #6dff9c) holds.
The first-word-medium rule now works on cards and covers Status, setup steps and the plans month. A latent bug that made the first word lighter in cards is fixed.
No word changed, no form changed, and nothing was removed.
weaknesses: The parent's big underlined typed count is gone, demoted to a small running-head readout. It is no longer a glanceable figure, and a judge who liked that element may see this as a loss.
At 80px the title is large. The 'Things to do' and 'Settings' pages push the lede into a narrow second column, and the lede sits far from the title on wide screens.

The bg #031415 is more saturated than the parent's #071212, because hue 200 needed more chroma to survive 8-bit rounding. It sits right at the signature's hue limit (199.95), and the surfaces are blue-slate beside a teal-black bg. That is a deliberate step, but it leans toward the 'tinted ground' that lost in earlier rounds.

The first-word weight difference (580 against 400) is hard to see at half size in serif card titles. It reads on the sans rows and at 100%. The first word can also be a small word ('The weekend digest').

The plans month's event chips now start with a heavier first word at 0.8rem, which makes the tiny chips busier. The phone's Chat, Plans and Status heads were not seen at phone width in the cards, only by the media rules.
I added the lead word to Status and Home setup rows, which goes a bit beyond the parent's original coverage.

elements.what: Giant condensed title over a running head: _ui.html `page_head` -> .head-run (.title-icon, .head-folio, .head-count) + .title-row h1 + .lede; CSS block '[head] A GIANT CONDENSED TITLE' at the end of sheet.css. The folio comes from the body's `in-<section>` class through --folio, and the trail's 3px bar is `.page-head::after`.

Ground one step cooler, neutrals one step warmer: palette tokens only (bg/bar #031415 at hue 199.95; surfaces, lines, edge and card-edge +17 degrees of hue; ink, ink-2, dim, faint, heading and secondary -11 degrees toward peach). No CSS.

First word medium (580), rest regular (400): `lead` macro (_lead.html) applied to rows on Home, Ideas, To do, Settings, Status lamps, setup steps and plans events. The CSS block '[list] a row's label' is last in sheet.css, with a span.lead reset.

name: Grid Console Typed Glass
tagline: Grid Console Lit Track with Home's question typed on the Next up tube under a block cursor and a lit lamp status line, light numerals one size up, and a faint band on every other row.
concept: The parent's heavy poster question moves off the box and onto the tube. Vera's presence and the date run along the top of the glass, the question is typed in VT323 with its key word lit and a block cursor after it, and a one-line lamp status sits under it. The box beside it becomes a plain field. Numerals go light and a step larger, so they read as figures in the margin, and the To do and Status rows alternate in a faint ground band.
companions: Nothing changed. The parent's companions stay: cyan accent and labels, the section and kind colours, amber for late and for the retrying or lost lamp on the glass.
decisions: [glass] The h1 and its label moved from _ask.html into the tube (home.html .tube-ask). The label keeps for=text, so the field is still labelled and the page still has one h1. The speaker row (presence, name, date) moved onto the glass as .tube-top. The donor's lamp status line (.glass-status) is read from talk.state and talk.note, never from a model. It is drawn in the parent's materials: phosphor-dim, the parent's own tube and hairline dashed divider, and no donor bezel, chin or colours.

Home's columns changed from 8/4 to 7/5 so the VT323 question fits at about 3.5rem. The box no longer stretches into a void: its textarea has a fixed 7.5rem minimum and the starters sit under it. On the phone the tube is ordered first, so the question comes before its field.

The parent's scanlined deep-green key word is replaced on the glass by a near-white core with a layered halo. A dim gradient word would have looked dimmer than the rest of the question on lit glass. The waiting_line under the box is dropped while a turn runs, because the lamp now says it.
The apostrophe is set in DM Mono (.ap) because VT323's curly apostrophe reads as a stray tick. Lessons say the VT323 apostrophe is a known flaw at this size, and this reduces it without removing it.

[type] --num-light: 300 on Archivo wdth 62 for .hc-figure, .fo-fig, .figure, .chip-day, month days, the kids' open count and the setup numbers, each about 10 to 15 percent larger. The small mono index numerals (the bar's 00-05, the folio over a title, .ix-no, .cell-no, .card-id) are also weight 300 and one step larger. Digits inside running text, such as the To do stamps, cannot be isolated in CSS and are unchanged.

[list] The band is applied to even rows of .line > li (To do page and Home's To do) and of table.data (Status), at 38 percent of surface toward surface-3 for plates and 55 percent for table rows. Hover goes to surface-3, so it stays lighter than the band. Grids of cards (Ideas, Coming up, Settings) are not banded, because every other card in a grid is not a row.
measures: The full render has 0 hard failures. The one WARN is the words changed: 8.8% on Home and 16.5% on Plans, a count that includes the parent's own rewording. ink_on_bg and brand_on_bg are both 14.95. The green share of colour is 54.8% on Home and the bright green is 3.8 per mille. hue_entropy is 0.518 on Home. dE kinds are 15.4 typical, 5.4 deutan and 6.4 protan; sections are 15.4, 5.4 and 8.2, so every floor is ok. The greeting's corner pixels are (4,9,6) at the top right and (15,23,24) at the bottom left, so there is no wash.
strengths: The question is now the machine's own, lit and typed, and it carries Vera's presence and a live status lamp in one place.
The Home squint test is clear: the lit tube is the focus and the box beside it is the plain field.
The light numerals are visible at half size in the chips (9, 17, 24), the head figures (12, 5, 4), the month's days and the kids' counts.
Every part has its own classes (.tube-ask, .glass-status, --num-light, the .line even rows) and could be lifted out.
The retrying and lost lamp states are amber, and the lamp swell respects reduced motion.
weaknesses: The poster question was the parent's strongest statement. In VT323 it is smaller, wraps to two lines, and the apostrophe still looks a little loose.
The left column is emptier: a plain box and chips, with a darker area below them.
Light 300 Archivo at wdth 62 is thinner than the heavy titles beside it. The count in the head and the date numerals lose some weight at a glance.
The row band is very faint. It is visible on the To do cards but easy to miss, and the Ideas, Coming up and Settings grids are not banded.
On the phone the tube sits first, which puts the field lower down, and Tab order no longer matches the visual order.
The words change measure (8.8% on Home, 16.5% on Plans) is not reduced by this mutant, and the waiting line under the box was removed.

elements.what: home.html .crt.tube-home > .tube-ask (p.tube-top with presence, .tube-who and .tube-date; h1.ask-question > label[for=text] + .glow + .crt-cursor; p.glass-status[data-state]). CSS is the [glass] block at the end of variants/r18-mut-11/sheet.css.

The --num-light: 300 numerals block in sheet.css. It covers .hc-figure, .fo-fig, .figure, .chip-day, table.month time, .kid-open .figure, .setup-list .number, .ix-no, .cell-no, .card-id, .page-title::before and the bar's a[data-no]::before, each one step larger.
The [list] banding block at the end of sheet.css: .line > li:not(.empty):nth-child(even), .checklist > li and .task-line > li.task, plus table.data even rows, with hover kept lighter than the band.

name: Grid Console Counted Keys
tagline: Grid Console Lit Track with a serif title and large counted figure over a hairline rule and its deck, the ways to start as a column of keys beside the box, and a deeper bezel and vent row on the monitors.
concept: Three changes to the parent, nothing else. Each page opens on a Fraunces title with a big mono count on its baseline and a small unit, then one hairline trail, with the line on what the page is for hanging under it. On wide screens Home's box has the ways to start as a column of raised keys at its right. The monitors' case gets a deeper bezel recess and a longer, clearer row of vent slots in the chin. It reads like a printed masthead over a console.
companions: Unchanged from the parent. The page colour (cyan accent, lilac Ideas, lemon To do, cyan Plans) colours the count and its underline and the hairline trail under the head, with the spine node now on that rule. The keys use the steel edge and the lit green chevron. The bezel is a lift of the existing graphite bezel. No new colour.
decisions: [head] The deck line moved out of .page-title into its own .deck block under the head row. The hairline is the parent's accent trail (.page-head::after, copied onto .deck::after), and the spine node (.deck::before, 78rem and up) now leaves from that rule. Heads with a deck turn the old bottom trail off (.has-deck). Plans has no deck, so it keeps the parent's bottom trail as its rule.

[head] Fraunces (SOFT 30, WONK 0, opsz 96, weight 560, up to 3.4rem) replaces the heavy condensed title on .page-head h1 only. Home's poster question and the section heads stay condensed. The digest warns that serif titles have faded six times, so this is a risk the panel can judge on the cards.

[head] The count uses the parent's Martian Mono, not the donor's IBM Plex Mono. It is larger (up to 3.2rem) at weight 400, with the unit as small mono caps. The parent's section-coloured underline and the Chat 'last 27 Sep' change line are kept. Chat's side column puts the count on the title line instead of below the deck.

[chat] _ask.html gets a div.ask-set around the form and the starters. From 64rem it is a two-column grid with an 11.25rem key column. The keys are full-width raised keys: surface gradient, steel edge, a 3px lip, the lit chevron, and a small 'Ways to start' label drawn by CSS ::before. Below 64rem the set is display:contents, so the phone and tablet chips are the parent's exactly. ask.js hiding the list still works, and :has() lets the box take the full width again.

[chat] The box is narrower beside the keys, so the 'Send where I am' tick moves to its own row under From, mic and Send. This matches the phone's arrangement. Without it, Send wrapped alone on a second row.

[glass] The parent already had a faint bezel and a 46px vent row. This is a bolder pass of the same idea: a groove, a lit lip and a second groove round the tube, and twelve 3px slots in a recessed dark plate (96px by 0.55rem). The chin is a little taller. Nothing else on the case changes. The monitor's lit corners, lamp, glass, scanlines and bloom are the parent's.
measures: The full render passes with 0 hard failures. The only WARN is the words-differ measure (worst page: Plans 16.5%, Home 7.7%). ink_on_bg and brand_on_bg are both 14.95:1 (the parent's). Green share of colour is 55% on Home, 51% on Ideas and about 39% on Chat. Hue entropy is 0.52 (Home), 0.49 (Ideas) and 0.51 (Chat). Section and kind colour distances are unchanged from the parent: typical 15.4, deuteranopia 5.4, protanopia 6.4 and 8.2. No sideways scroll. Greeting corner samples on the Home shot are (4,9,6) at (1150,120) and (9,17,16) at (100,640). Both are plain dark ground, because at 1280 wide (1150,120) falls on the Next up monitor's case, not the old wash. The new Home layout contains no corner wash.
strengths: Every page head changes at a glance: a serif title with a large lilac, cyan or lemon count, then one rule, then the deck. This shows on Home's neighbours (Ideas, Status, To do, Settings, Chat) and on all the cards.
The deck under the rule makes the head a clean masthead with the page's spine node on the rule. The parent's lede-beside-title row is gone.
The keys column fills the height of Home's box and reads as keys to press. It leaves the phone untouched.
The case change is lifted into its own selectors, so the monitors, gauge and radar pick it up together.
Each slot lives in its own classes (.deck, .ask-set, the .crt chin block) and can be lifted out on its own.
weaknesses: The glass change was already half in the parent, so the visible difference is a deeper, longer pass of the same idea. At half size the twelve vent slots read as a faint dotted strip.
Serif titles have faded six times in earlier rounds. Here the serif loses the heavy condensed Grid voice of the parent's heads, and now differs from the condensed section heads under it.

The narrow box on Home pushes 'Send where I am' to its own row. The box is shorter than the parent's and the ways to start are two-line keys. Chat shows no ways to start, so the column only appears on Home.
'Ways to start' is a CSS ::before label, and it adds a few words to the page-words measure.
The head ends with a hairline and the deck, so there is slightly less air than the parent's single-line head on Plans-like pages. Plans, with no deck, keeps its old bottom trail.

elements.what: Serif page title (Fraunces 560) with a large mono counted figure, a small unit and a hairline trail, and the deck under the rule. In templates/_ui.html page_head (header.has-deck, div.deck > p.lede); CSS in the sheet's [head] block (.page-head h1, .hc-figure, .hc-unit, .deck, .deck::before, .deck::after).

The ways to start as a column of raised keys beside the box from 64rem, with a 'Ways to start' label and the Send-where tick on its own row. In templates/_ask.html (div.ask-set); CSS in the [chat] block (.ask-set, .ask-set > .starters, its a, ::before).

A deeper bezel recess round the tube (groove, lit lip, groove) and a row of twelve slots in a recessed plate in the chin. CSS only, in the [glass] block of the sheet (.crt > .crt-tube box-shadow, .crt background layers).

name: Green Desk
tagline: A 1984 desktop on a green tube: striped title bars that are scanlines, putty monitors, and a dotted time-ruler spine every page hangs from.
concept: The first graphical desktops (System 1, GEM) redrawn in phosphor. Every panel is a window with a scanline-striped title bar and a close box. A dotted mauve time-ruler runs down the left, lit green at NOW, and each window, day, task and chat speaker branches off it. It should feel like a small beige machine whose screen is the family's calendar. This revision gives the lit windows weight and lets the secondary ones recede, so the system reads on dense pages as well as on Home.
companions: Dusty mauve (hue 338; spine #966a89, words #dab4cd) is time and order only: the ruler, branches, due-day ticks, chat time stamps, ids, 'in 6 days' tags. Putty #6e6a5c is the monitors' plastic. Each section colours its title-bar stripes, icon tile and active tab (lilac Ideas, cyan Plans, lemon To do, pink wishes, amber Family, and amber for today and for warnings). A warning is an amber title bar and nothing else. Green is the machine's light: the mark, the default button, the key word, focus, lamps, NOW, the monitors, the pixel glass of Vera's tile, and the thin line under her name in the chat.
decisions: Frame weight now says how much of the page a window is. The primary windows (the question, Coming up, To do, the chat box, the month grid) keep the 2px card-edge outline and the hard offset shadow, which I lifted from #1a2420 to #232e29 so it reads on #070a09. Everything else is a 1px line-2 hairline with no shadow, and thickens inward to its section's colour when pointed at. I took this from the critic's 'too much frame on dense pages' note.

The window idea now reaches the pages where it vanished, using one title-bar system (close box, stripes, label). Plans' month head is the grid's bar, with the month name centred between stripes and Earlier/Later at the right. Each task's head is its bar, and the tick box is the close box, which fills when pressed. Each Settings tile has a bar carrying its name. This needed two small template copies, settings.html and tasks.html, and no words were removed.

Timeline made true beyond Coming up. On To do each task hangs from the spine with its due day ('27 Sep') as a mauve tick under the branch. On Chat each speaker is a tile sitting on the rail itself, with the time stamp hung under the tile like a ruler mark, so the bubble header holds only the name. Under 56rem the stamp goes back into the bubble header.
Settings sub-pages get their branches back. At 62rem and wider the branch goes to the page list, which is now a framed window. Below that, every box gets its own.

Gutter 5.6rem on desktop (a little wider for the chat stamps). At 56rem and below it collapses to 1.15rem, with the rail at 0.6rem and the branch reduced to a hollow node. Home's form gets its width back and Send goes full width on a phone. A phone had the ruler, and the tablet band now does too.

Type steps. Pixelify Sans is kept at 16px and up for titles, bars, nav and buttons, where it is Chicago. Everything smaller, such as eyebrows, labels, legends, fact terms, tags, kinds, table heads and the chip month, moves to Atkinson Hyperlegible bold with tracking. Silkscreen only appears at 16px (NOW, month numerals, setup step numbers) and 24px (date leaf numerals), which are multiples of its 8px grid. Every text is at least 12.8px (the old 11.5px floor is gone). Mauve words lifted to #dab4cd (10.8:1 on bg), and Vera's date line is softened so it does not shout over the headline.

Press targets: --hit is 2.75rem and goes on buttons, fields, tabs, starters, nav, menu rows, checkbox labels and summaries. The task tick gets a 44px hit area through ::after. Inline links in rows widen with padding that does not grow the row.

Icons snapped to a 24px grid: title, kind and section tiles are 3.5rem or 3rem with a 24px icon, pixelated rendering, and a 1px lit top-left edge like a desktop icon. Four key icons (ideas bulb, plans calendar, to-do ticks, wishes gift) are redrawn as true 1-bit pixel art on a 12x12 grid in the sprite.

Colour clutter cut to one hue per window. 'Finish setting up' and the Status warnings are an amber or red title bar with a hairline frame and ink-coloured links. Maya and Theo are ink with a small pink square. The family's chat bubbles lose their amber outline.

Light stays where the phosphor is. The putty monitors, tube, bloom, sweep and blips are untouched. The title-bar stripes are the tube's scanlines: primary windows 1px-in-3 at 70%, secondary 1px-in-4, and the Status trio at 35%.
measures: The final full render has 0 hard failures. The one WARN is Plans at 13.9% of words differing: the demo date moved the month, and the new due-day ticks on To do add a few. ink_on_bg 16.21, brand_on_bg 15.56, brand_neon_vs_today 1.0. Green share of colour: home 43.6%, ideas 67.9%, chat 48.7%, status 48.6%. Hue entropy: home 0.67, ideas 0.48, chat 0.58, status 0.69. dE kinds typ/deu/pro is 14.6/5.6/6.0, and sections typ/deu/pro is 14.6/5.6/6.0. The greeting corner pixel was not sampled, because the clean sheet has no wash. Smallest text is now at least 12.5px. Press targets under 44px on Home fell to 21 of 55, with 3 under 24.
strengths: One window system with real reach: the same bar (close box, stripes, label) now appears on Home panels, the Status trio, Settings tiles, the month grid, every task, and the chat bubbles. A new page would inherit it.
The timeline is no longer a Home-only decoration. Chat is a literal time ruler with speaker tiles on the rail, To do hangs its tasks by due day, and Coming up keeps its day branches.
Frame weight hierarchy: a few heavy outlined windows with hard shadows, and a calm field of hairlines. Dense pages are lighter than before.
Putty monitors with the lit radar and Next up keep the full original tube effect (scanlines, bloom, caret, power lamp) in grounded plastic.

Colour has jobs. Mauve means time, section colour means which part of the app, amber means warning or today, and green means the machine's light, including Vera's tile in the chat. Home reads as greyscale with a few lit things.
Hit areas and the phone are much better: the spine collapses to a node column, Send is full width, and starters, tabs and ticks reach 44px.
weaknesses: Under 56rem the due-day tick moves into the task's title bar, and the chat time stamp returns to the bubble header. The ruler-tick metaphor is a wide-screen feature only.
I did not add a separate 'Open - 4' title bar over the To do list. The cards are the windows, and a plain '4 shown' mauve count sits above them. The critic's list-level bar is only half done.

The pixel icons are only four of the sprite. At the 20px nav size they land on 1.67px per pixel, so they look slightly uneven beside the Lucide icons. The rest of the sprite is still square-capped outline, which reads as 'outlined', not 1-bit.

The 2px frame and hard shadow are still heavier than the style guidelines on the primary windows, and the Status trio keeps its stripes at 35%. The page is lighter overall but still busier than a flat dark UI.
Chat bubbles are capped at 40rem, so a wide desktop leaves a quiet empty right half. It is a deliberate measure but looks sparse.
Some inline links are still under 44px (21 of 55 targets on Home, 3 under 24px). Lists of text links in dense rows are enlarged only by invisible padding.

The new template copies (settings.html, tasks.html) move words around slightly, and the due-day ticks add duplicate date words, which show up in the word-difference count. I did not check General settings sub-pages in a render, because the harness no longer shoots them. Their branches are written but not seen.
revisions: Acted on: carried the window bar through Plans' month, To do tasks and Settings tiles.
Acted on: due-day ticks on To do, and chat time stamps and speaker tiles moved onto the spine.
Acted on: the settings sub-page branches are back, on the page list at wide widths and on each box at narrow ones.
Acted on: frame weight (1px hairlines on secondary windows, 2px plus shadow on primary ones), the shadow lifted to #232e29, and quieter stripes on secondary bars including the Status trio.
Acted on: type legibility. Silkscreen is only at 16 or 24px, small caps eyebrows are bold Atkinson with tracking, mauve words are lighter (#dab4cd), and small text is raised to 13px or more.
Acted on: gutter collapse at 56rem and below, and 44px press targets on tick, tabs, starters, mic and checkbox rows.
Acted on: colour clutter. Warnings are a title bar tint only, Maya and Theo are ink with a pink square, and the family's bubbles lose their amber outline.
Acted on: icon tiles on a 24px grid with a lit top-left edge, and four icons redrawn as 1-bit pixel art.
Acted on: chat typesetting with a 40rem measure, 16px/1.55 body, a 13px tracked time, and Vera's thin phosphor line under her name.

Partly declined: 'keep Pixelify only at 20px and up'. I kept it at 16px and up for bars, nav and buttons, because that is the System-1 voice and it stayed legible in the renders. I moved everything under 16px to the reading face instead.
Partly declined: a separate bar and branch for the To do list as a whole. Each task being its own window with its own branch fits the timeline better than one box.
Declined: dropping the offset shadow entirely. The lifted shadow stays on the primary windows and monitors, because the hard shadow is the idea.
Declined: Vera's bubbles in --bubble-them. I kept the bubble fills as they were, and made her distinct with the green line and her glass tile.
crit: Carry the window idea through the pages where it vanishes: Plans' month grid, the To do rows and the Settings tiles are plain bordered boxes with no title bar, close box or branch. Give main > .panel, .month-head + grid, each task list and .settings tiles the same bar (a 14px stripe row with a centred label such as 'October 2026', 'Open - 4', 'General') and one hollow-square branch to the spine. Also restore the branches switched off on settings sub-pages, or the spine reads as a Home-only decoration.

Make 'timeline' true beyond Coming up: on To do, hang each task off the spine at its due date (a small mauve date tick left of .task, ordered by due, with 'was due 6 days ago' as the tick label) and on Plans' list view show the same date leaves; on Chat the day-time stamps ('27 Sep, 19:47') should sit on the spine as ruler ticks rather than inside every bubble header. Otherwise drop the claim to 'ruler' and keep it as a structural device.

Fix legibility of the pixel faces: Silkscreen at 12px for eyebrows ('NEXT UP', 'SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER', 'ON THE RADAR', month strip numerals) and the tracked caps in the Vera title bar should be 14-16px or switched to the plain sans with 0.08em tracking; keep Pixelify only at 20px and up (titles, 'What's on your mind?'). Body, ids (#4, #1) and tags should use tabular figures in the sans. Raise the mauve small text (ids, 'in 6 days', counts) from #cba3be at 11px to 12.5-13px or lighten to about #dcb7cf so it holds 4.5:1.

Reduce the frame weight on dense pages (Status, Settings, To do): 2px --card-edge borders plus a hard offset shadow plus a striped bar on every box is too much. Use 1px --line-2 borders and the 2px edge only on the focused or the top-level window, keep the offset shadow (#1a2420 is nearly invisible against #070a09, so lift it to about #232e29 or drop it) on the primary window and monitors only. Let the Status 'Who answers/Keys/Connected to' trio drop their title-bar stripes to 1px-in-4 at 35% so the bars read as title bars, not flat bands at half size.

Win back width and touch targets on the phone: the 1.9rem spine gutter plus a 2px frame leaves the Home form cramped, with the Send button and the 'Remind me to...' / 'We should try...' starters wrapping in the squeeze. Collapse the gutter to 1rem (spine at left: 0.5rem, branches 0.5rem long) under 640px and on tablets (<900px). Raise ticks (.tick, 27px), tabs and starters to a 44px hit area with padding or ::after, and give the mic and the checkbox rows the same.

Cut the leftover colour clutter that undermines the 1-bit read: on Home the amber 'Finish setting up' box, pink Maya/Theo links, the mauve branches and the lilac tab all sit together; keep one accent per window (title-bar stripes and icon tile in the section colour, border in --line-2), make warnings an amber title bar only, and let 'Maya' and 'Theo' be ink with a small pink dot. Aim for greyscale plus one hue per window plus green for light, which also makes the 1-bit twist honest.

Make the icons pixel-true: the Lucide sprite with square caps still reads outlined. Snap icon tiles to a 16 or 24px grid with image-rendering: pixelated at the tile (title-icon, .kind tiles, .places icons), draw a few key ones (ideas bulb, plans calendar, to-do ticks, wishes gift) as 1-bit, and give the tile an inset 1px highlight so it looks like a desktop icon; the idea cards on Home are the best place to show it.

Tighten Chat and form typesetting: the thread is a column of full-width bordered boxes with tiny 12px headers, so give the bubbles a 36rem measure with the speaker's S/A avatar tile on the spine, set body at 16px/1.55, the sender line in the sans 13px with a tracked time, and keep Vera's bubbles in --bubble-them with a thin green title-bar line only when she is the one speaking, so lit green means her screen.

firstDraft.name: Green Desk
firstDraft.concept: The first graphical desktops (Mac System 1, GEM) redrawn in phosphor: every panel is a window with a striped title bar (the stripes are the tube's scanlines), a close box, square corners and a hard offset shadow; buttons are rounded rectangles with the default button's ring; selection is inverse. A timeline is the spine of every page: a dotted time-ruler runs down the left, lit green at NOW where the page begins, and each window (and each day in Coming up) branches off it with a hollow square node. It feels like sitting at a small beige machine whose screen is the family's calendar.

elements.what: Window title bar system: .wbar (new), .panel > h2:first-child, .section-head, .month-head h2, .tasks .task-head, .said-by. Close box and 1px-in-3 or 1px-in-4 scanline stripes via --bars/--bars-o, tinted by --stripe from the section's --accent; primary windows 2px outline plus hard shadow, secondary windows 1px line-2.

The spine: main::before is the dotted ruler, main::after is the lit stretch, .page-head::before is the NOW tag, and the hollow-square branch ::before sits on each top-level window, each day and each task. Mauve is reserved for time and order.

.in-chat .thread:not(.brief) log: speaker tile on the rail, branch line to a 40rem window, time stamp (.said-by > strong + span) hung under the tile, Vera's thin phosphor line under her name via .said-bot.

To do task window (.tasks > li.card with .task-head as bar and tick as close box) plus .due-tick in tasks.html; Coming up agenda days with calendar-leaf .chip tiles and their branches; Lately added desktop icons.

Type steps: Pixelify Sans at 16px and up for bars, nav and buttons; Atkinson Hyperlegible bold, tracked, for eyebrows, labels and tags; Silkscreen at 16 or 24px only; mono tabular figures for ids and times; 40rem chat measure.

One hue per window: section colour on stripes and icon tile, warnings as a tinted title bar (.setup, .trouble, .attention, .section-card.look), mauve for time, putty for the monitors, green for the machine's light.

Sunken fields with a lit focus ring and green caret, inverse hover on secondary buttons and tabs, square checkboxes with a drawn tick, the ringed default button, and a --hit 2.75rem press target (the tick's ::after widens it).
.page-head: 3.5rem 24px-grid icon tile with a lit corner edge, Pixelify title, dotted running rule, NOW tag and a branch from the spine.
Putty monitors (.crt): compact-Mac case, floppy slot in the chin, tube, bloom, scanlines, sweep and blips kept at full strength.
